title: Comparison of sensorimotor and supportive insoles for children with flat feet, to the use of a neutral insole - a randomized, prospective, controlled survey
summary:
The aim of the study is to test the effectiveness of various insole therapies. Sensorimotor, supportive and neutral insoles are used for this purpose.
The study is carried out on children aged 5-12 years who have a 'flexible flat foot': The heel appears to be bent outwards (kinked foot) and the arch of the foot is flattened (flat foot). The child's flexible flat foot can cause complaints such as foot or knee pain. The foot malposition is usually noticed when the child is observed while walking. The soles of the shoes are often particularly worn on the inner edge due to the misalignment of the feet. Doctors often prescribe different types of insoles.
In future, we would like to be in a position to recommend, or advise against specific treatment for children with flat feet. 
Each study participant is assigned to one of three groups. Each group receives one of the types of insoles mentioned above. 
First, a clinical examination of the feet is carried out. Then the parents will fill out a questionnaire together with their child. This is to record the subjective well-being of the child. The insoles are customized to the child's feet after biomechanical measurements. The insoles used are approved medical products that are established as standard therapy. The clinical examinations are carried out according to the usual standardized procedure. No x-rays are taken.
An examination period of 12 months is planned. 
There may be follow-up examinations to look at the long-term results. 
The aim of this study is to determine whether insoles are effective and, if so, which type of insoles best corrects the deformity of the foot.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children with a flexible flat foot
- Children from 5 - 12 years
- Boys and girls
- Neuromotoric healthy children
Exclusion criteria:
- Rigid flat foot
- Other structural foot deformities (congenital/acquired)
- Neurological, genetic underlying diseases
- Foot injury, foot surgery in the last 6 months
- Lack of consent to participate
